Buckle 2.8 x 2.0625 in, keepers 0.46 x 2.0625 in 2.22 in either side of the buckle's centre, eight eyelets 0.21 in across (columns 2.75 and 4.53 in from the buckle's centre, rows 1.12 in apart) are measured on the Class A guard figure and the Class B long-sleeve figure of the Honor Guard guidance at the figures' hardware scale (the belt's own 2 1/16 in = 96 px, 46.5 px/in; the 7/8 in coat button is 41 px, the same scale). The belt runs from torso edge to torso edge of garment-blues-class-b-shirt-male at the belt line (the figures' belt ends at the torso edge on both). Same box as garment-blues-class-b-shirt-male.","provenance":"in-house vector. Measured on the four figures of \"CAP Honor Guard Uniform Guidance\" (page 4 rendered at 6x, flat colours so each part is a mask): belt outline height 96.1 px (Class A guard) and 95.6 px (Class B long) = 2 1/16 in; buckle plate 128 x 94 px, keepers 19 x 93 px, keeper centres 104 px (2.22 in) either side of the buckle's centre, eyelets 10 x 11 px in two columns (86 px apart at 312/398 px and 654/735 px) and two rows 52 px apart. Height: the belt's centre is the centre of the sheet's own blue belt (y 24.20 in): the waist where the shirt meets the trousers; the figure puts the belt just under the fourth button, the sheet draws a longer shirt, and 9.6.7.2 says the belt is worn as with the Service Dress coat. The buckle is on the button column (figure: 3 px, 0.08 in, from it). g.title: White web pistol belt, 2 1/16 in wide (CAPR 39-1 9.6.7.6), worn tight between the second and third button of the coat, at the waist of the shirt (9.6.7.1.2, 9.6.7.2)
